activity_statements.statement: discovers, develops, manufactures, and commercializes prescription medicines across oncology, vaccines, infectious diseases, cardiometabolic, immunology, and neuroscience
develops and distributes vaccines for humans (including Gardasil for HPV, Varivax for varicella) and has been doing so for over 130 years
employs approximately 24,700 people in R&D and invested $15.8 billion in research and development in 2025
manufactures and sells veterinary medicines and vaccines through Merck Animal Health for livestock and companion animals
partners with external biotech companies through licensing and business development to build a hybrid pipeline of internally-discovered and externally-sourced drug candidates
conducts global clinical trials to generate evidence for regulatory submissions across FDA, EMA, and other health authorities

name_reality_gap: Merck is labeled 'Healthcare Biotech & Pharmaceuticals' which is accurate. The less-visible reality is that Merck operates a major Animal Health segment (veterinary drugs and vaccines for livestock and pets) alongside its human health business, and that Keytruda (cancer immunotherapy) has become one of the world's best-selling drugs, making Merck an oncology powerhouse as much as a diversified pharma company.
extraction_notes: Good sources available from merck.com. R&D investment ($15.8B in 2025) and R&D headcount (~24.7K) taken directly from research page. Segment weight estimates based on known Merck reporting (Animal Health is approximately 15% of revenue).
